title: Understanding L0 Regularization
text: L0 regularization limits the number of non-zero parameters in the model. In this case, it allows all $$5$$ parameters to be non-zero. This means the model can use all features without any penalty.

title: Logistic Regression Basics
text: Logistic regression predicts probabilities that are then rounded to $$0$$ or $$1$$. The sigmoid function, \(\sigma(z)\), is used to map any real-valued number into the \(0,1\) range.

title: Sigmoid Function Insight
text: The sigmoid function \(\sigma(z)\) is defined as \(1/(1+e**{-z})\). When $$\(z=0\)$$, $$\(\sigma(0)=0.5\)$$. This is the threshold for classifying predictions as $$0$$ or $$1$$.

title: Applying L0 Regularization
text: Since $$\(k=5\)$$, all parameters can be non-zero. This means the model can perfectly fit the training data without any regularization penalty.

title: Misclassification Count
text: With all parameters available and no penalty, the model can perfectly classify the training data. How many points are misclassified?
